title.narrative: WASH Rehabilitation of Flood-affected schools in Karary Locality

description.narrative:
Torrential rains that began in Sudan in late July and early August 2013 caused severe material damage, casualties, and affected an estimated 340,000 people in the country. The floods are reportedly the worst seen in the recent history of the country, particulary in Khartoum state, with more urban areas affected compared to the notorious 1988 floods. Over 140,000 primary school-aged children were affected by the floods across Sudan - the majority in Khartoum State. During the flooding, schools in Khartoum State were on holiday for the Eid Festival. Children returned to school, only to find that classrooms, latrines, and school grounds had been damaged or totally destroyed by high winds, rainwater, flooding and stagnant water. Some schools in different areas of Khartoum remained closed due to major damage, and pupils were transferred to nearby schools, causing already flood-damaged classrooms to be overcrowded. In order to address the limited space and lack of latrines, some schools are taking shifts while others have shortened the school day. In the 200 assessed schools, 810 classrooms were found destroyed or damaged, while 313 latrines were rendered out of use by the floods. As a result of the floods, it is estimated that about 14,743 children across the 200 schools are not as yet accessing safe and quality education due to the unsafe environment – 56% of them being girls. Many children, in particular girls, remain at risk of dropping out or not returning to school due to lack of sanitation facilities and the generally unhygienic and unsafe situation in the schools. Mujaddidun was part of the above joint assessment. It is clear from the assessments that there is a need to restore facilities immediately in order to enable pupils to access quality and education in safe environments. As a result, the following priorities were identified by all assessment groups: - Gender-sensitive latrine construction - Rehabilitation of classrooms and fences - Water facilities rehabilitation - Public health activities.
This project has secured fund from UNICEF that will go towards WASH rehabilitation and activities in 4 schools targeting 1,189 school children (482 girls and 707 boys). will build on the existing SDN011 project to expanding the work
